title: Chief articles suffice for faith — yet every believer must press on in the Word
source_text: XLII. Neque tamen, quum dicunt ad fidem sufficere explicitam & expressam summorum aliquot fidei capitum notitiam, propterea existimant pium & laudabile esse in ejusmodi qualicunque notitia acquiescere, nec cognitionem ampliorem quaerere. Quamvis enim paucorum articulorum fides explicita & expressa tanquam ad salutem plane necessaria exigatur, pretendunt tamen unumquemque teneri omnem operam adhibere, ut pro vocationis modo, in doctrina salutis magis magisque proficiat, pleniusque & copiosius in verbo Dei instruatur. Ad quod sedulo fideles hortatur Apostolus, ut praesertim videre est in epistola ad Colossenses; ubi optat ut sint Instructi in charitate, & in omnes divitias plenitudinis intellectus, in agnitionem mysterii Dei ac Patris & Christi Jesu. Et monet ac praecipit, ut Christi verbum habitet in nobis abundanter, in omni sapientia, nos mutuo docendo & commonfaciendo Psalmis, hymnis & canticis spiritualibus: cap. 2. & 3. Unde est quod scribens ad Hebraeos ipsos graviter increpat, quod cum deberent esse magistri propter tempus, rursum tamen indigerent, ut docerentur elementa exordii sermonum Dei; & opus haberent lacte, ac non solido cibo. Hebr. 5. Ex quibus merito colligunt Reformati graviter errare & peccare illos qui, sub praetextu fidei implicitae, crassam & stupidam plebis ignorantiam fovent. Quae omnia tam clare & aperte, & tam unanimi consensu a Doctoribus Reformatis traduntur, ut minime necessarium sit eorum testimonia hac in parte citare.
pass_a_gloss: Nor yet, when they say that explicit and express knowledge of some few chief heads of faith suffices for faith, do they therefore think it pious and praiseworthy to rest in such knowledge of whatever sort, and not to seek fuller cognition. For although explicit and express faith of a few articles is required as altogether necessary unto salvation, they nevertheless maintain that each one is bound to apply every effort, that according to the manner of his calling he may more and more advance in the doctrine of salvation, and be more fully and richly instructed in the word of God. To which the Apostle diligently exhorts the faithful, as is especially to be seen in the epistle to the Colossians; where he desires that they be Instructed in charity, and unto all the riches of the fullness of understanding, unto the acknowledgment of the mystery of God and the Father and of Christ Jesus. And he warns and commands that the word of Christ dwell in us abundantly, in all wisdom, teaching and admonishing one another with Psalms, hymns and spiritual songs: chapters 2 and 3. Whence it is that writing to the Hebrews he gravely rebukes them, that when they ought to be teachers because of the time, they nevertheless again needed to be taught the elements of the beginning of the oracles of God; and had need of milk, and not of solid food. Hebrews 5. From which the Reformed rightly gather that those gravely err and sin who, under pretext of implicit faith, foster the crass and stupid ignorance of the people. Which things are all handed down by the Reformed Doctors so clearly and openly, and with such unanimous consent, that it is by no means necessary to cite their testimonies in this part.
pass_b_english: Explicit knowledge of a few chief heads suffices for faith — but not as a pious rest-stop.
Each must press on in saving doctrine according to calling.
Colossians: abound in the word; Hebrews 5: leave milk for solid food.
Fostering people’s crass ignorance under ‘implicit faith’ is grave error.
